key_insight: The paper replaces biased mini-batch Cox normalizer estimates with a softplus-based grouped surrogate that enables unbiased stochastic gradients and sharper convergence guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale survival analysis more practical by reducing optimization bias and memory/computation costs while preserving the full Cox estimator’s asymptotic behavior.
method: Introduce one auxiliary scalar per LogSumExp normalizer and optimize a softplus surrogate with unbiased single-sample gradients.
Prove improved optimization rates for smooth convex objectives and a last-iterate guarantee under strong convexity in the main variable.
For Cox regression, group neighboring failures to share auxiliary variables, using uniform score/curvature bounds to control approximation error.
evidence_signal: Experiments on synthetic and real survival datasets with slowly decreasing risk sets show favorable performance compared with stochastic baselines, and the compressed estimator matches the full estimator’s asymptotic distribution.
watch_item: The grouped compression introduces approximation error, so performance depends on how well neighboring failures can be clustered and on the risk-set structure.
paper_title: Scalable Cox Regression via Grouped Risk Sets and Sharper LogSumExp Rates
